title: Mamdani says feds have abdicated on AI, urges New Yorkers to push back
slides: Why is Mamdani calling out the feds on AI?
He says Washington has abdicated its oversight role
New Yorkers may face AI harms with no federal backstop
Local pressure could shape rules cities actually enforce
Ask one local official where they stand on AI
thread_text:
1. Mamdani Blames Feds on AI

New York Assembly member Zohran Mamdani says Washington has abandoned its oversight role, leaving cities to fend for themselves on artificial intelligence.

2. Washington Abdicates Oversight

Mamdani argues federal agencies have refused to set rules for AI, creating a vacuum that local governments must fill without resources or authority.

3. New Yorkers Face AI Harms

Without a federal backstop, New Yorkers could encounter biased algorithms, unsafe systems, and opaque decisions with no clear path to recourse.

4. Local Pressure Shapes Rules

City-level activism and public scrutiny can influence the AI rules that municipalities actually enforce, even as federal policy stalls.

5. Ask Your Local Official

Contact your city council member or county supervisor today and ask one direct question: where do you stand on AI oversight?

instagram.caption:
Zohran Mamdani says Washington walked away from its job of overseeing AI — and left cities holding the bag.

His point: federal agencies won't set the rules, so local governments have to fill the gap without the resources or authority to do it.

That means biased algorithms and opaque decisions could reach New Yorkers with no clear path to push back.

If you publish or build with AI tools, the rules you'll actually live under may get written at city hall, not in DC.

So here's one question worth asking your city council member this week: where do you stand on AI oversight? 🗽🔍📣
